key_insight: Raman scattering reveals that phonon behavior in metal halide perovskites is strongly shaped by coupling between the inorganic lattice and A-site cation dynamics, with the central peak mainly arising from disorder-induced second-order acoustic-phonon scattering.
engineering_relevance: Understanding these lattice interactions helps engineers interpret Raman spectra, diagnose structural disorder, and better link composition/temperature to stability and optoelectronic performance in perovskite solar materials.
method: Review of experimental Raman evidence across metal halide perovskites
Comparison of coupling mechanisms: hydrogen bonding vs steric hindrance
Analysis of the zero-shift central peak and its disorder-based origin
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes existing Raman measurements and supports the central-peak interpretation by analogy to other disordered semiconductor systems such as Ge quantum-dot stacks and GaAs/AlAs superlattices.
watch_item: Raman features can be strongly influenced by phase, temperature, and disorder, so assigning peaks without careful context may lead to incorrect conclusions about lattice dynamics.
paper_title: Phonon Interactions in Metal Halide Perovskites elucidated by Raman Scattering
